title: これ・それ・あれ・どれ
pattern: これ / それ / あれ は ＿＿ です
meaning_en: Points to a thing: this (near me), that (near you), that (over there), which.
explanation: Japanese has three distance words for things: これ (near the speaker), それ (near the listener) and あれ (far from both). どれ asks "which one?" among three or more.
They stand alone as the topic of a sentence: これ は ほん です (This is a book). To ask about a thing say これ は なん です か.
It is the position of the thing that matters: if you pick up an item, it is これ for you and それ for the shop assistant.
structure_notes: これ/それ/あれ は + noun + です. They replace a noun; they cannot be placed before a noun.
common_mistakes: Putting これ before a noun (use この).
Using これ for something that is near the listener.

title: この・その・あの・どの
pattern: この / その / あの + noun
meaning_en: This / that / that over there / which + noun.
explanation: この, その, あの and どの always come directly before a noun: この ケーキ (this cake), あの ひと (that person over there), どの ひと (which person).
They follow the same distance pattern as これ・それ・あれ・どれ. They cannot stand alone.
No の is needed between them and the noun.
structure_notes: この/その/あの/どの + noun.
common_mistakes: Using これ before a noun.
Adding の between この and the noun.
